cards.title: Collocations, idioms and similes
rule: A **collocation** is a pair of words that naturally go together: *make a decision, do homework, commit a crime, pay attention, take an exam, keep a promise, heavy rain, strong tea*.
You cannot translate them word for word. ✗ *do a decision, give attention, strong rain*.
An **idiom** has a meaning different from its words: *break the ice* = start a friendly conversation; *once in a blue moon* = very rarely; *a piece of cake* = very easy.
A **simile** compares with **as … as** or **like**: *as busy as a bee, as brave as a lion, sleep like a log*.

cards.pattern: make / do / take / pay + noun  ·  as + adjective + as + noun

cards.title: Notes
body: **make** = create (a decision, a mistake, a plan, progress, noise); **do** = activity/work (homework, the dishes, an exercise, your best).
Learn collocations in pairs and write your own sentence with each one.
Idioms are used in speaking and stories; in formal essays use plain words.

cards.title: Worked practice
cards.problem: The school board decided to ________ progress on the new laboratory construction project.

steps.text: **Step 1: Look at the sentence.** The noun 'progress' requires the verb 'make' to form the standard English collocation: make + progress.
**Step 2: Watch out for the trap.** Students often choose 'do' because they translate 'ዕብየት ገይሮም' (made progress) directly using the Tigrinya verb 'ገበረ' (to do).

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The school board decided to ________ progress on the new laboratory construction project.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Look at the sentence**
The noun 'progress' requires the verb 'make' to form the standard English collocation: make + progress.

**Step 2: Watch out for the trap**
Students often choose 'do' (Option A) because they translate 'ዕብየት ገይሮም' (made progress) directly using the Tigrinya verb 'ገበረ' (to do). Option B 'make' is correct.

**Step 3: In Tigrinya**
'Progress' (ዕብየት/ምስጓም) ዝብል ስም ምስ 'make' ዝብል ግሲ ጥራይ እዩ ዝጣመር (make progress - Option B)። ተማሃሮ 'ዕብየት ገይሩ' ንምባል 'do progress' ክብሉ ይጋገዩ እዮም፤ እዚ ግን ናይ ቀጥታዊ ትርጉም መጻወድያ እዩ።

cards.title: Worked practice
cards.problem: Because of the ________ rain, the regional football championship was postponed until next week.

steps.text: **Step 1: Look at the sentence.** The noun 'rain' is modified by the adjective 'heavy' to describe high volume, forming the fixed collocation: heavy + rain.
**Step 2: Watch out for the trap.** Students often choose 'strong' because they translate 'ሓያል ዝናብ' (strong rain) directly from Tigrinya.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Because of the ________ rain, the regional football championship was postponed until next week.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Look at the sentence**
The noun 'rain' is modified by the adjective 'heavy' to describe high volume, forming the fixed collocation: heavy + rain.

**Step 2: Watch out for the trap**
Students often choose 'strong' (Option A) because they translate 'ሓያል ዝናብ' (strong rain) directly from Tigrinya. In English, 'strong' is used for wind, while 'heavy' is strictly used for rain. Option B is correct.

**Step 3: In Tigrinya**
ኣብ እንግሊዘኛ ምስ 'rain' (ዝናብ) ዝኸይድ ናይ መጠን መግለጺ ቃል 'heavy' ጥራይ እዩ (heavy rain - Option B - ከቢድ ዝናብ)። ኣብ ትግርኛ 'ሓያል ዝናብ' ስለ ዝበሃል፡ ተማሃሮ 'strong rain' ብምባል ክጋገዩ ይረኣዩ እዮም፤ እዚ ግን ጌጋ ጥምረት እዩ።

cards.title: Worked practice
cards.problem: The final biology practical exam was ________; almost every student scored full marks.

steps.text: **Step 1: Look at the sentence.** The context 'almost every student scored full marks' indicates the exam was extremely easy.
We need the idiomatic expression meaning very easy.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The final biology practical exam was ________; almost every student scored full marks.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Look at the sentence**
The context 'almost every student scored full marks' indicates the exam was extremely easy. We need the idiomatic expression meaning very easy.

**Step 2: Watch out for the trap**
Option A 'a piece of cake' is the correct idiom. Option D 'burning the midnight oil' means studying late, which is related to exams but does not fit the description of the test itself.

**Step 3: In Tigrinya**
'A piece of cake' (ኣዝዩ ቀሊል) ዝብል ምስላዊ ኣዘራርባ፡ ሓደ ተግባር ወይ ፈተና ብቀሊሉ ክዕመም ከሎ ንምግላጽ የገልግል። እቶም ተመሃሮ ምሉእ ነጥቢ ስለ ዘምጽኡ፡ እቲ ፈተና ኣዝዩ ቀሊል ነይሩ፤ ስለዚ ቅኑዕ መልሲ Option A እዩ።

questions.q: True or false: "fast food" and "quick meal" are both natural collocations.
questions.label: 20. True or false: "fast food" and "quick meal" are both natural collocations.
why: True. English speakers say "fast food" and "a quick meal".
"quick food" and "a fast meal" sound unnatural.
So the statement is true.
